issues.description: Inner blocking read loop has no timeout or process-exit check, trading a truncation race for a potential deadlock
issues.detail: Once the fd is flipped to blocking, the original safety nets (poll timeout, check_process_exited) are gone. If the writer hangs without closing the FIFO, the parent blocks forever. All three reviewers flagged this as the central regression: an intermittent truncation has been swapped for a guaranteed hang on writer-stall.

issues.description: fcntl mode flip lacks error handling and has no cleanup on exception
issues.detail: F_GETFL/F_SETFL can raise OSError, and if F_SETFL fails the fd is left in an inconsistent state. The function also silently mutates fifo_fd's blocking mode without restoring it, affecting any caller that reuses the descriptor. Wrap with try/except and restore the original flags on exit.

issues.description: No regression test exercises the original race or the new blocking path
issues.detail: An intermittent JSONDecodeError at ~86KB is exactly the failure that silently returns after a future refactor. Correctness rests entirely on a prose appeal to POSIX semantics. Add a fault-injection test that writes a large payload and closes the writer to lock in the fix.

issues.description: BlockingIOError handler silently reduced to pass, dropping has_blocking_error semantics
issues.detail: Previously the handler used content and has_blocking_error to detect a closed file; now it just passes. Either the variable is dead and should be removed in a separate cleanup, or downstream semantics have quietly changed. Conflating the fix with a silent behavior change makes the diff hard to review.

issues.description: Patch bundles the race fix with deletion of a MacOS-specific workaround
issues.detail: The removed block existed because POSIX-blocking behavior was not observed on MacOS FIFOs. The commit asserts POSIX semantics solve the problem but offers no evidence the MacOS path is subsumed. Split the patch or justify why the workaround is now obsolete.

issues.description: Two read loops with different EOF semantics complect the read protocol
issues.detail: A non-blocking outer loop wrapping a blocking inner loop with its own EOF logic is two state machines for one job. Extract the drain-to-EOF logic into a named helper (e.g. _drain_blocking(fifo_fd) -> bytes) so the outer loop is readable and the unit-testable surface is obvious.

synthesis.summary: The panel converges on NEEDS-WORK. The diagnosis (non-blocking read sees zero before kernel buffers drain) is correct and the switch-to-blocking strategy has the right shape, but the implementation trades an intermittent truncation for a potential deadlock by removing the poll/process-exit backstop on the blocking path. Secondary problems compound it: fcntl calls lack error handling and cleanup, the BlockingIOError branch silently changed semantics, a MacOS-specific workaround was deleted without justification, and no regression test was added for a race that already shipped. The fix should restore a timeout or process-exit check on the blocking read, harden fcntl error handling, separate the MacOS-workaround removal, and land with a fault-injection test.
